title: Lens shift (verticals stay vertical) with setViewOffset
summary: Cut-aways and AI images often use a shifted lens: high horizon, vertical verticals. Look level, then S.cam.setViewOffset(1920, 1080, 0, offY, 1920, 1080) after S.camera().

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

doc.when: The reference's verticals are parallel but its vanishing point is far from the frame centre.
doc.avoid: Pitching the camera to move the horizon (verticals lean up to ~70 px at the frame edges).
gotchas: setViewOffset survives the engine's updateProjectionMatrix calls.
S.camera has no shift parameter yet (engine request: S.camera({ shift })); a solver must either fit shift or keep it at 0.

params.offY: pixels at 1080 (206 in the tunnel shot)

problem.symptom: Horizon high (vanishing point at y~315/1080) but every vertical perfectly vertical; a pitched camera leans the verticals.
problem.cause: The reference is drawn with a shifted (off-axis) lens; S.camera only has p/l/fov/roll.
problem.fix: Look level, then S.cam.setViewOffset with the solved shift.
problem.detect: Solver fits markedly better with shift as a free parameter (dig: 29 vs 35 px).
